title: INTENT: Out-of-Sample, Out-of-Time, and Cold-Start Evaluation on User Event Sequences
abstract: arXiv:2611.13069v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Banks now train foundation models on ordered sequences of customer events such as transactions, app sessions, and authorizations. Deployed, such a model predicts forward in time, often for customers and merchants absent from training, yet each is evaluated on private data, so no two can be compared. Public benchmarks for such sequences rarely test a period the model has not seen; recommendation studies usually hold out each user's last events instead. We present INTENT (INTEraction, Novelty, and Transfer evaluation for next-action prediction), a public benchmark that scores a model in seven cells defined by whether the user, the period, and the target item appeared in training. An audit of 59 public dataset families retains five datasets; the most common defect is the lack of a calendar timestamp that orders events. No date lies within the time span of all five datasets, so each is split at its own cutoff, chosen by one rule fixed before

translated_title: INTENT：用户事件序列上的样本外、时间外与冷启动评估
translated_abstract: 银行如今在客户事件的有序序列上训练基础模型，例如交易、应用会话和授权。部署后，这类模型需要在时间上向前预测，且预测对象往往是训练中未出现的客户和商家；然而每个模型都在各自的私有数据上评估，因而无法相互比较。针对此类序列的公共基准很少测试模型未见过的时期；推荐系统研究则通常只保留每个用户的最后几个事件作为测试。我们提出了INTENT（面向下一动作预测的交互、新颖性与迁移评估），这是一个公开基准，根据用户、时期和目标项目是否出现在训练中，将模型评估划分为七种情形进行打分。对59个公开数据集家族的审计最终保留了五个数据集；最常见的缺陷是缺少用于对事件排序的日历时间戳。由于没有任何日期落在所有五个数据集共同的时间跨度内，因此每个数据集都按照事先固定的统一规则在其各自的截止时间点进行切分。
tldr: 提出了INTENT这一公开基准，根据用户、时期与目标项目是否在训练中出现，将用户事件序列上的下一动作预测模型划分到七种情形下评估，从而统一衡量其样本外、时间外与冷启动泛化能力。
en_tdlr: INTENT is a public benchmark that evaluates next-action prediction models on user event sequences across seven cells defined by whether the user, the time period, and the target item appeared in training, enabling unified measurement of out-of-sample, out-of-time, and cold-start generalization.
